learning: Iteration 7 showed that kp 2.5 removes slalom line loss on the 0.10 track but does not recover oval progress above 0.35. The test here is whether an intermediate kp can hold both.
notes: Controller for the Builder's wheel_track 0.10 platform, with kp set to 2.75 between the measured kp 2.5 (line loss 0.0, oval progress 0.30) and kp 3.0 (line loss 0.35, oval progress 0.28) points. Geometry is passed through unchanged.
rationale: Iteration 7 already raced the kp 2.5 test on this same wheel_track 0.10 platform (entityR2B, 79.60). It removed slalom line loss (0.0 per run) but left oval progress at 0.30, below the 0.35 threshold in the Builder's revert rule, and max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.063 m. Iteration 6 (kp 3.0) gave slalom line loss 0.35 and oval progress 0.28. Progress is therefore not recovered by kp 2.5, and line loss is set by kp on this track. I keep the supplied geometry (wheel_track 0.10, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18, sensors at y 0.03, 16 mm footprints) because the Builder's proposal is the input I must build. I interpolate to kp 2.75, which sits between the two measured points, to see whether line loss stays near 0.1 while oval progress rises above 0.35. kd 0.3, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.2 and last_direction are unchanged, so kp is the only controller variable. No outcome is claimed for this candidate, which has not raced. Expected result: slalom line loss between 0.0 and 0.35, oval progress between 0.30 and 0.55, and max_error still near 0.063 m, which would confirm that gain balance is the limit.
